definition: A software application designed specifically for use on mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets.
extendedDefinition: A mobile app is software designed for smartphones and tablets, delivered through app stores or as progressive web applications, and increasingly the primary interface for field workers, customers, and on-call staff. Mobile apps differ from desktop tools in interaction constraints, offline behavior, notification patterns, and device security management. Buyers evaluating mobile coverage should check which workflows are truly mobile-native, whether offline access works in the field, and how push notifications integrate with existing channels. Mobile apps also raise device management questions: enrollment, remote wipe, and compliance policies matter when corporate data leaves the office. Development quality varies widely, so trials should include real-device testing of the specific tasks the team performs daily. The practical benchmark is whether the app reduces time-to-response or replaces paper processes, not whether a mobile interface exists in the product marketing.
